arxiv-2008-07782.title: Molecular picture for X 0 ​ ( 2900 ) X_{0}(2900) and X 1 ​ ( 2900 ) X_{1}(2900)
arxiv-2008-07782.creator: Jun He 1, Dian-Yong Chen 2
arxiv-2008-07782.description: Abstract Inspired by the newly observed X 0 ​ ( 2900 ) X_{0}(2900) and X 1 ​ ( 2900 ) X_{1}(2900) at LHCb, the K ∗ ​ D ¯ ∗ K^{*}\bar{D}^{*} and K ​ D ¯ 1 K\bar{D}_{1} interactions are studied in the quasipotential Bethe-Salpeter equation approach combined with the one-boson-exchange model.

arxiv-2104-06227.title: Weak Measurement of Berry’s Phase
arxiv-2104-06227.creator: Z. Gedik
arxiv-2104-06227.description: Abstract Quantum measurements can be generalized to include complex quantities. It is possible to relate the quantum weak values of projection operators to the third order Bargmann invariants. The argument of the weak value becomes, up to a sign, equal to the Berry’s phase associated with the three state vectors.

arxiv-2104-10264.title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: A search for Planet 9
arxiv-2104-10264.creator: Sigurd Naess, Simone Aiola, Nick Battaglia, Richard J. Bond, Erminia Calabrese, Steve K. Choi, Nicholas F. Cothard, Mark Halpern, J. Colin Hill, Brian J. Koopman, Mark Devlin, Jeff McMahon, Simon Dicker, Adriaan J. Duivenvoorden, Jo Dunkley, Valentina Fanfani, Simone Ferraro, Patricio A. Gallardo, Y
arxiv-2104-10264.description: Abstract We use Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) observations at 98 GHz (2015–2019), 150 GHz (2013–2019) and 229 GHz (2017–2019) to perform a blind shift-and-stack search for Planet 9. The search explores distances from 300 AU to 2000 AU and velocities up to 6.3 arcmin per year, depending on the distance ( r r ).

arxiv-2206-07405.title: ParamNet: A Multi-Layer Parametric Network for Joint Channel Estimation and Symbol Detection
arxiv-2206-07405.creator: Vincent Choqueuse, Alexandru Frunza, Adel Belouchrani, Stéphane Azou, Pascal Morel
arxiv-2206-07405.description: Abstract This paper proposes a parametric-based network architecture for joint channel estimation and data detection in communications systems with hardware impairments. This architecture is composed of a data-augmented layer, a custom soft thresholding function, and several linear layers modeling the effect of channel effects and hardware impairments.

arxiv-2207-12392.title: Self-Distilled Vision Transformer for Domain Generalization
arxiv-2207-12392.creator: Maryam Sultana, Muzammal Naseer, Muhammad Haris Khan, Salman Khan, Fahad Shahbaz Khan
arxiv-2207-12392.description: Abstract In the recent past, several domain generalization (DG) methods have been proposed, showing encouraging performance, however, almost all of them build on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). There is little to no progress on studying the DG performance of vision transformers (ViTs), which are challenging the supremacy of CNNs on standard benchmarks, often built on i.i.d assumption.

arxiv-2305-07735.title: Faint but not forgotten. I. First results from a search for astrospheres around AGB stars in the far-ultraviolet
arxiv-2305-07735.creator: Raghvendra Sahai, Benjamin Stenger
arxiv-2305-07735.description: Abstract Using the GALEX archive, we have discovered extended structures around 10 AGB stars (out of a total 92 searched) emitting in the far-ultraviolet (FUV) band. In all but one, we find the typical morphology expected for a spherical wind moving relative to, and interacting with the ISM to produce an astrosphere.

arxiv-2305-13712.title: Knowledge of Knowledge: Exploring Known-Unknowns Uncertainty with Large Language Models
arxiv-2305-13712.creator: Alfonso Amayuelas, Kyle Wong, Liangming Pang, Wenhu Chen, William Wang
arxiv-2305-13712.description: Abstract This paper investigates the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the context of understanding their knowledge and uncertainty over questions. Specifically, we focus on addressing known-unknown questions, characterized by high uncertainty due to the absence of definitive answers.

arxiv-2307-07557.title: Photon and dilepton emission anisotropy for a magnetized quark-gluon plasma
arxiv-2307-07557.creator: Xinyang Wang, Igor A. Shovkovy
arxiv-2307-07557.description: Abstract We study the higher-order anisotropy coefficients v 4 v_{4} and v 6 v_{6} in the photon and dilepton emission from a hot magnetized quark-gluon plasma. Together with the earlier predictions for v 2 v_{2} , these results show a distinctive pattern of the anisotropy coefficients in several kinematic regimes.

arxiv-2506-05541.title: The coordinate functions of the Heighway dragon curve
arxiv-2506-05541.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . In this work, we study properties of the coordinate functions x θ x_{\theta} and y θ y_{\theta} of the dragon curve associated with the angle π 3 < θ < 5 ​ π 3 \frac{\pi}{3}<\theta<\frac{5\pi}{3} , and we prove that the box-counting dimension of its graph is equal to 1 − log ⁡ cos ⁡ α log ⁡ 2 1-\frac{\log\cos\alpha}{\log 2} , where α = π − θ 2 \alpha=\frac{\pi-\theta}{2} .

arxiv-2508-15955.title: Advancements in Degenerate Distributed Feedback Lasing
arxiv-2508-15955.creator: Albert Herrero-Parareda, Nathaniel Furman, and Filippo Capolino
arxiv-2508-15955.description: Abstract We advance the concept of degenerate distributed feedback (DDFB) lasing in a double grating photonic structure that operates near a degenerate band edge (DBE) to achieve a robust single-frequency lasing regime. The DBE is an exceptional point of degeneracy (EPD) of fourth order involving four coalescing Bloch eigenmodes.

arxiv-2509-08840.title: Cosmological Time Dilation and the Hubble Tension in the meVSL Model
arxiv-2509-08840.creator: Seokcheon Lee
arxiv-2509-08840.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Seokcheon Lee. We investigate the relation between cosmological time dilation (CTD), photon–baryon decoupling, and the Hubble tension in the minimally extended varying–speed–of–light (meVSL) framework. The generalized cosmological time (GCT) framework distinguishes cross-epoch temporal standardization from local interaction laws. For the diagnostic early-Universe calculation, the hydrogen recombination history is taken to be GR-like, while the homogeneous meVSL opacity prescription retains the correlated b b dependence of the dimensional Thomson cross section.

pmc-10519359.title: PSY–PSYR peptide–receptor pairs control the trade-off between plant growth and stress response
pmc-10519359.creator: Quy Thi Cam Nguyen, Jungmook Kim
pmc-10519359.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Leucine-rich repeat-receptor kinases (LRR-RKs) perceive various endogenous peptide hormones that control plant growth and development. However, the majority of corresponding ligands and their direct ligand-binding receptors have not been identified yet. A recent study demonstrated that three LRR-RK PLANT PEPTIDE CONTAINING SULFATED TYROSINE RECEPTORS (PSYRs) act as ligand-receptors of the PSY family peptides that mediate the trade-off between the optimal plant growth and stress tolerance responses.

pmc-10982614.title: Time to treat the climate and nature crisis as one indivisible global health emergency
pmc-10982614.creator: Chris Zielinski
pmc-10982614.description: ding to the climate crisis and the nature crisis as if they were separate challenges. This is a dangerous mistake. The 28th Conference of the Parties (COP) on climate change is about to be held in Dubai while the 16th COP on biodiversity is due to be held in Turkey in 2024.

pmc-11319042.title: Equity considerations in clinical practice guidelines for traumatic brain injury and the criminal justice system: A systematic review
pmc-11319042.creator: Zoe Colclough, Maria Jennifer Estrella, Julie Michele Joyce, Sara Hanafy, Jessica Babineau, Angela Colantonio, Vincy Chan
pmc-11319042.description: BackgroundTraumatic brain injury (TBI) is disproportionately prevalent among individuals who intersect or are involved with the criminal justice system (CJS). In the absence of appropriate care, TBI-related impairments, intersecting social determinants of health, and the lack of TBI awareness in CJS settings can lead to lengthened sentences, serious disciplinary charges, and recidivism.

pmc-11416712.title: Iatrogenic acute type A aortic dissection during catheter ablation for idiopathic ventricular premature contraction
pmc-11416712.creator: Shinichi Ishida, Yoshio Takemoto, Ryutaro Kimata, Kei Yagami
pmc-11416712.description: Acute aortic dissection type A during cardiac catheterization has been reported as a rare but fatal complication. We present a case of acute aortic dissection type A occurring during catheter manipulation in the ascending aorta during mapping of ventricular premature contraction via the retrograde approach.

pmc-12730071.title: Implementing Self-Regulated Learning in Classrooms: Connecting What Primary School Teachers Think and Do Through Video-Based Observations and Interviews
pmc-12730071.creator: Lies Backers, Hilde Van Keer, Stella Vosniadou
pmc-12730071.description: Self-regulated learning (SRL) is crucial for effective learning, supporting academic achievement and lifelong competencies. Fostering SRL in primary education is important, yet teachers’ understanding and use of strategies are underexplored. This study provides an innovative, multi-method investigation of whether and how primary school teachers’ knowledge and beliefs about SRL align with their classroom practices.

pmc-13138616.title: Cardiovascular risk assessment with SCORE2 and targeted health dialogues in primary care patients with mental illness
pmc-13138616.creator: Veronica Milos-Nymberg, Hanna Glock, Miriam Pikkemaat, Moa Wolff, Beata Borgström Bolmsjö, Peter Nymberg
pmc-13138616.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPatients with mental illness face a higher risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), mainly due to unhealthy lifestyle habits. The CVD risk assessment tool Systematic COronary Risk Evaluation 2 (SCORE2) does not assess modifiable lifestyle factors beyond smoking. In Sweden, Targeted Health Dialogues (THD) are used in primary care as a structured, person-centred approach designed to evaluate lifestyle behaviours that influence CVD risk.

pmc-13297647.title: Quantum Computing for Optimal Dispatch of Virtual Power Plants Under Wind and Solar Uncertainty
pmc-13297647.creator: Ningqiao Liu, Yuxin Zhang, Zhihang Liu, Chao Zheng
pmc-13297647.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The modern power system is characterized by large-scale networks, diverse types of sources and loads, and complex grid structures. Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) are proposed to address the operation problem after the integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs). Optimization problems in the VPP operation are predominantly mixed-integer programming (MIP) problems belonging to the class of NP-hard problems, motivating the application of quantum computers.

pmc-13311996.title: DCAF7 enhances atherosclerosis in vascular endothelial cells by promoting SLC40A1 transcription through facilitating TNF-mediated NF-κB function
pmc-13311996.creator: Sien Guo, Peng Yan, Gengchen Niu, Biqi Li, Ni Wu, Qisen Yao, Shengyuan Wang, Chongyuan Hu, Yisheng Zheng, Yihe Yan, Huafu Li, Chunming Wang

pmc-13400201.title: Vacuum-pulsating ultrasound synergy for efficient extraction of bioactive substances from Lonicera japonica
pmc-13400201.creator: Dong Wang, Chun Wang, Yifan Zhao, Yao Niu, Zhiyun Chen, Cunliang Li, Pei Li, Yong Wang, Yuejin Yuan, Yang Sun
pmc-13400201.description: This study presents a vacuum pulsating ultrasound extraction (VP-UE) technique for extracting bioactive compounds (chlorogenic acid(CGA),total flavonoids(TF),polysaccharides(PS)) from uncrushed and microcrushed Lonicera japonica (Flower bud) under laboratory-scale conditions. By combining vacuum pulsation and ultrasonic cavitation, VP-UE creates a bimodal pore structure (macropores and micropores) in the material, enhancing mass transfer and solvent contact.

pmc-13619366.title: Exploring Symptom Domains of Postoperative Bowel Dysfunction by Integrating LARS and Wexner Scores: A Longitudinal Factor‐Analytic Study
pmc-13619366.creator: Yoshiko Matsumoto, Issei Takeshita, Keiichi Shiokawa, Kurumi Sahara, Taro Munechika, Ken Nagata, Hideki Nagano, Hiroyuki Takahashi, Suguru Hasegawa

pmc-13677432.title: Rumble Recognition: a gastrointestinal sound discrimination task to measure gastrointestinal interoception
pmc-13677432.creator: Hannah S. Savage, Beth F. Longley, Hugo D. Critchley, Lydia J. Hickman, Wilson P. H. Lim, Adrian E. Yoris, Edwin S. Dalmaijer, Camilla L. Nord, Sarah N. Garfinkel
pmc-13677432.description: Gastrointestinal interoception is the sensing, interpretation and integration of signals originating from the gut. In contrast to chemosensory aspects of gut-brain signalling, perceptual aspects of gastrointestinal viscerosensation and visceromotor control have received relatively little attention despite links to physical and mental health and wellbeing.
